title: Microsoft Purview: sensitivity label protection policies for Microsoft Fabric items
summary: The briefing passes: its cited documentation supports the access restrictions, exceptions, licensing caveat and consumption meter, and its roadmap facts match the record. Minor corrections should acknowledge the separate SQL database guidance on retaining read versus full-control permissions, complete two paths and align the checklist with the controls table.

claims.quote: Microsoft Purview compliance portal: Information Protection - Sensitivity labels protection policy support for Microsoft Fabric

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview protection policies control access to Fabric items through their sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview protection access control policies (protection policies) enable organizations to control access to items in Fabric using sensitivity labels.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Labels; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Each Fabric protection policy is associated with one sensitivity label.
claims.quote: You can select only one label per policy.

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph; Why it matters; controls[0]
claims.claim: Users and groups specified in a policy retain the permissions they already have on items carrying its label.
claims.quote: The policy controls access to an item that has the associated label by allowing users and groups specified in the policy to retain permissions they have on the item, while blocking access for everyone else.
claims.fix: Keep the statement attributed to the Fabric overview, but add: 'The separate SQL database guidance distinguishes retained read access from retained full control: the read-access option removes other item permissions, and users not specified in the full-control option lose the Write item permission.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/database/sql/protect-databases-with-protection-policies. That page says 'Any other permissions the specified users have on the item get removed' for the read-access option, unlike the general overview's wording.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Other users are denied access to labelled items, subject to the documented label-issuer and native-item creator exceptions.
claims.quote: The policy controls access to an item that has the associated label by allowing users and groups specified in the policy to retain permissions they have on the item, while blocking access for everyone else.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The user who last applied the policy's label is not denied access even when not specified in the policy.
claims.quote: A protection policy doesn't apply to a label issuer. That is, the user that last applied a label associated with a protection policy to an item won't be denied access to that item, even if they aren't specified in the policy.

claims.where: summary; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: For automatically labelled native Fabric items with no designated label issuer, the creator is not restricted by protection policies.
claims.quote: For native Fabric item types, if the label is applied automatically by the system—such as in the case of downstream inheritance—and there is no designated label issuer, the user who created the artifact will not be restricted by protection policies.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Who configures; controls[0].note; controls[2]
claims.claim: Creating protection policies in the Microsoft Purview portal requires at least Information Protection Admin.
claims.quote: You must have at least the Information Protection Admin role to create protection policies in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.where: Scope: Who configures; controls[2].note
claims.claim: Information Protection Admin is assigned by default under the Compliance Administrator role group.
claims.quote: The Information Protection Admin role is assigned by default under the Compliance Administrator role group.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Items; controls[0].scope
claims.claim: A Fabric protection policy applies to supported item types in all workspaces.
claims.quote: The policy will apply to supported item types in all workspaces.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Items; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Supported native Fabric items include lakehouses, notebooks, pipelines and other core Fabric assets.
claims.quote: Protection policies are supported for all native Fabric item types, including lakehouses, notebooks, pipelines, and other core Fabric assets.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Power BI semantic models support protection policies.
claims.quote: Additionally, protection policies are supported for Power BI semantic models.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope
claims.claim: Power BI reports and dashboards are not currently supported by these protection policies.
claims.quote: Other Power BI item types, such as reports and dashboards, aren't currently supported.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A newly created policy can take up to 24 hours to start detecting and protecting items carrying its label.
claims.quote: After a policy has been created, it can take up to 24 hours for it to start detecting and protecting items labeled with the sensitivity label that was associated with the policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Status; controls[0].note; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn documents protection policies and identifies the Purview policy page as preview, despite the roadmap's In development status.
claims.quote: Open the Protection policies (preview) page in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Protection policy restrictions require an administrator to create and turn on a policy; the default state is admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: Protection policies ensure that enterprise admins must authorize data access for a sensitivity label. After you enable these policies, access control is automatically imposed whenever Information Protection detects sensitive information.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Service principals cannot be added directly to protection policies through the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Service principals can't be added to the policy directly in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Service principals needing protected-item access can be placed in a security group included in the policy.
claims.quote: If service principals need to access items protected by the protection policy you're configuring, add them to an Azure security group that you'll include in the policy.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Service principals with existing access are denied when not on the allowed list, potentially breaking applications that access semantic models.
claims.quote: If you don't add service principals to the allowed list of users, service principals that currently have access to data will be denied access, potentially causing your application to break. For example, service principals might be used for application authentication to access semantic models.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope: Limits; Open questions
claims.claim: Fabric protection policies do not support guest or external users.
claims.quote: Protection policies for Fabric don't support guest/external users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Deployment pipelines and Git integration use workspace permissions rather than item-level protection policy permissions.
claims.quote: Protection policies don't integrate with Fabric CI/CD solutions. Deployment pipelines and Git integration use only workspace permissions, not item-level permissions from protection policy labels.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope: Limits
claims.claim: Up to 50 protection policies can be created in the tenant.
claims.quote: Up to 50 protection policies can be created.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope: Limits; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Up to 100 users and groups can be added to a protection policy.
claims.quote: Up to 100 users and groups can be added to a protection policy.

claims.where: Scope: Labels; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A label used by a Fabric protection policy must be scoped to Files & other data assets.
claims.quote: "Appropriately configured" in the context of protection policies for Fabric means that when the label was configured, it was scoped to Files & other data assets, and its protection settings were set to include Control access

claims.where: Scope: Labels; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The label's protection settings must include Control access.
claims.quote: its protection settings were set to include Control access

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisite in Fabric; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Allow users to apply sensitivity labels for content must be enabled for protection policy enforcement and all sensitivity-label-related policy enforcement in Fabric.
claims.quote: For protection policies to be enforced in Fabric, the Fabric tenant setting Allow users to apply sensitivity labels for content must be enabled. This setting is required for all sensitivity label related policy enforcement in Fabric

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1]; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The Fabric sensitivity labelling tenant setting lets administrators define who can apply and change labels, including specific security groups.
claims.quote: Select Specific security groups if you want to allow this capability for only certain users. Make sure that the security group(s) you specify contain only users who you want to be able to apply and change sensitivity labels on items.

claims.where: Governance controls: first paragraph
claims.claim: Users allowed to apply or change sensitivity labels also need Create and Edit permissions on the item.
claims.quote: Users who this setting allows to apply and change sensitivity labels must also have Create and Edit permissions on any item they wish to apply or change a label on.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Spend control; Open questions
claims.claim: The Usage center documentation does not specify the effect of pausing Information Protection on Fabric protection policy enforcement.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview Usage center Information Protection pause enforcement API PowerShell; Purview Information Protection pausing enforcement. Read purview/purview-billing-usage and purview/purview-billing-models; no Fabric enforcement effect stated.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The printed Purview path reaches the Fabric protection policy wizard's Add users and groups control.
claims.quote: On the Choose the sensitivity label used to detect sensitive items page, select + Add sensitivity label ... On the Define access control settings page ... Select Add users and groups
claims.fix: Use 'Information Protection > Policies > Protection policies > + New protection policy > Name and describe your protection policy > Choose the sensitivity label used to detect sensitive items > + Add sensitivity label > label > Choose data sources to apply the policy > Microsoft Fabric > Define access control settings > Add users and groups'. The omitted wizard headings and label selection are non-blocking. The navigation and + New protection policy are also documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/data-gov-protection-policy, which is already cited.
